text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read, understand, and maintain. For example, you might rename unclear variables, break a long function into smaller ones, or remove repeated logic. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs; the program should behave exactly the same after the changes. It also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when code is written quickly without care. Although refactoring takes time, it makes future changes safer and faster, so most developers consider it a valuable habit.
